solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Ardent male advance between two singles, one on date

indicators.note: something placed between two things sits inside the pair, so the first pieces go inside the other

parts.note: a single is one, I in Roman numerals; two of them flank the rest
D is the abbreviation for date
M is the abbreviation for male
to make a pass is to make an amorous advance

explanation.surface: A passionate man makes his move on two single women, one of them on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: A pass is an amorous advance, which fits the dating surface; the singles are not unattached people but the numeral I twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Impassioned means filled with strong feeling, a close synonym of ardent.

clue.text: Pre-emptively raiding timber pile, one dry within

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for the hyphenated adjective

indicators.note: within says the following pieces sit inside the preceding word for a pile

parts.note: fir is a softwood used as timber
TT, teetotal, describes someone who is dry

explanation.surface: Raiders strike first at a timber pile, one dry piece hidden inside.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, teetotal, is the crossword convention for dry; the answer is a hyphenated adjective, like first-strike.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-attack strategy hits the enemy before they can strike, the same idea as a pre-emptive strike.

clue.text: Describing fine mosaic rock, 'turned off-colour', we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the letters come from the sound of a phrase rather than its spelling

parts.note: to turn off-colour is to fall ill

explanation.surface: A geologist describes a finely patterned rock that has changed colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Off-colour is British for slightly unwell, so turned off-colour is fell sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Felsic describes igneous rock rich in feldspar and silica, often fine-grained with a mosaic texture.

clue.text: Whistler 'Golden Maiden' getting a make-over?

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A painting by Whistler called 'Golden Maiden' is being restored.
explanation.walkthrough: Whistler looks like the painter James McNeill Whistler, but it is a referee.
explanation.definitionFit: A reform is an improvement by change, which is what a make-over provides.

clue.text: Some additions to kerosene as fuel

indicators.note: some of the words means only a part of the run of letters is taken

explanation.surface: Adding something to kerosene to make it burn as fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoke a fire is to fuel it, adding coal or wood to keep it burning.

clue.text: Creatures clad in seaweed, with time extremely pungent

parts.note: a tangie is an Orkney water spirit that appears as a man covered in seaweed
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Seaweed-covered creatures that smell very strongly after a while.
explanation.walkthrough: Tangie is a Chambers word from Orkney and Shetland folklore, so the first part is a cryptic description rather than a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangiest is the superlative of tangy, so it means having the sharpest, strongest smell or taste.

clue.text: Ceremonial staff, one from Siam (as was) — how nice!

parts.note: Tai is a variant of Thai, a native of Siam, the old name for Thailand
an exclamation of pleasure or satisfaction

explanation.surface: A Thai visitor admires a ceremonial staff with delight.
explanation.definitionFit: A taiaha is a long Maori fighting staff, now carried on ceremonial occasions.

clue.text: Old granny providing crib for toddler?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old woman, an archaic sense
second meaning: a literal translation used by students
third meaning: a small child just learning to walk

explanation.surface: Grandma supplies a cot for the little one.
explanation.walkthrough: Crib looks like a baby's cot next to granny and toddler, but it is a student's translation aid; this is really three definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists the word as an old woman, a crib or literal translation, and a toddling child.

clue.text: Perfect glance going wrong, one getting caught

indicators.note: being caught means being held inside, so the single letter sits within the others
a plan going wrong falls into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A perfect glance between two people goes wrong when one is caught looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Angelic means like an angel, flawless in goodness or beauty, so perfect.

clue.text: Coat in wax American cactus? Rescue works

parts.note: to cere is to wrap in waxed cloth
a second, confirming route: the letters of rescue reworked spell the same word

explanation.surface: Coat an American cactus in wax, and the rescue will succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: Azed gives two routes to the same answer: the waxing-plus-American charade, and 'Rescue works', the letters of rescue reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereus is a genus of tall columnar cacti native to the Americas.

clue.text: Plateau thrilled mates going round Spain

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so the country letter goes inside
thrilled people are excited and stirred up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Excited friends touring Spain reach a high plateau.
explanation.definitionFit: A meseta is a high flat tableland, the name used for the central plateau of Spain.

clue.text: E.g. orpiment from NZ, mined with care

indicators.note: mined letters have been dug up and churned about, so they come out in a different order

explanation.surface: Orpiment dug carefully from a New Zealand mine.
explanation.definitionFit: Zarnec is an old name for orpiment, a yellow arsenic mineral, so orpiment is an example of it.

clue.text: Tricks in groups of three are daunting

definitions.note: a plural verb phrase for the base verb

parts.note: ternate means arranged in threes, as of leaves

explanation.surface: Card tricks performed in threes are intimidating to watch.
explanation.definitionFit: To consternate is to fill with dismay, so things that consternate are daunting.

clue.text: River turns entering artificial lake — bridge now abandoned?

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the first piece is placed within the lake

parts.note: a pond is a small man-made lake

indicators.note: a thing that turns faces back the other way, so the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall

explanation.surface: A river winds into a man-made lake, and the old bridge across it is no longer used.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge looks like a river crossing in this setting, but it is the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: Plafond was a French card game, a forerunner of contract bridge, now no longer played.

clue.text: Court order: one like this restricts onset of bullying

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem in, so the initial goes inside the other piece
the onset of anything is its beginning, so only the first letter is used

explanation.surface: A court order like this one is meant to curb bullying from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO, Anti-Social Behaviour Order, was a British civil order (abolished 2014) restricting a person's antisocial conduct, such as bullying neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: It was an order made by a magistrates' court against a named person, so a court order.

clue.text: Glossy fabric lending special allure to one at secondary school?

parts.note: SA is short for sex appeal
a secondary school pupil is a teenager

explanation.surface: A shiny fabric gives a teenage pupil extra glamour.
explanation.definitionFit: Sateen is a cotton cloth woven to have a glossy, satin-like finish.

clue.text: Law scrolls: one falling in fire's ruined

indicators.note: falling in means dropping inside, so the single letter goes into the word
something ruined is wrecked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Sacred scrolls of the Law are destroyed when one falls into a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Sifrei is the plural of sefer, a scroll of Jewish scripture such as the Torah, which is the Law.

clue.text: Fairly new rule he's infringed cutting angle

indicators.note: cutting into something puts a piece inside it
an infringed rule is broken, so the letters are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A newish rule he breaks cuts into the angler's catch.
explanation.walkthrough: Angle looks like geometry beside rule, but it is the verb to fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Freshish means somewhat fresh, so fairly new.

clue.text: Anatomical opening, vaguely bluish, seeping a bit of blood

indicators.note: vaguely suggests a loose, imprecise arrangement, so the letters are reordered
something seeping leaks away, so a letter is lost
a bit of a word is a small part of it, here its opening letter

explanation.surface: A medical description of a wound that is faintly blue and oozing blood.
explanation.walkthrough: Take B out of BLUISH and rearrange the remaining LUISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A hilus is the notch where vessels and nerves enter an organ such as the kidney or lung.

clue.text: Have a distinct feeling about lawyer in brief really losing head

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: quite can mean really, as in quite sure

explanation.surface: A lawyer in a brief case has a strong instinct, really, but loses his head.
explanation.definitionFit: Attuite is a rare psychology verb meaning to perceive something by attuition, a distinct sensory awareness short of full perception.

clue.text: Potter etc with arrangement round Chinese plants

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters surround the plant word
an arrangement puts things in a fresh order, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: ramis are ramie plants, also called China grass

explanation.surface: A potter and others arrange pots around some Chinese plants.
explanation.walkthrough: Potter looks like a gardener's verb next to plants, but it is the noun for a pottery maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceramist makes ceramics, so a potter is an example.

clue.text: In short, an unknown quantity, neither one nor the other

explanation.surface: Put briefly, someone hard to pin down is neither one thing nor another.
explanation.definitionFit: Intersex describes a person or animal with characteristics of both sexes, so not wholly male or female.

clue.text: Raised pistol to catch something small but valuable

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word turns it upside down, reading it bottom to top

explanation.surface: A gunman raises a pistol to grab a small valuable item.
explanation.definitionFit: A nugget is a small lump of gold, or anything small and precious, such as a nugget of wisdom.

clue.text: Retaining base, king twice in check (6, two words)

indicators.note: retaining means holding on to something within, so the base letter goes inside

parts.note: R is short for rex, king
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A chess game where the base is kept and the king is put in check twice.
explanation.walkthrough: Check looks like chess talk alongside king, but it is the definition, meaning restrain.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in a horse is to pull it up, so to check or restrain.

clue.text: Pigment that's brown or black turning livid round stone

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black

indicators.note: round says the anger word surrounds the stone abbreviation

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, a British weight

explanation.surface: A paint that is brown or black and turns a livid shade around a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown or black reads as one colour description, but black only gives a letter; turning livid is showing anger. A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Bistre is a brown pigment made from wood soot, used in ink drawings.

clue.text: Thessalian ruler, jealous when roused, without justice

indicators.note: roused means stirred up, so the remaining letters are stirred into a new order
without means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for justice, a judge

explanation.surface: An ancient Greek king flies into a jealous rage and acts unjustly.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Aeolus, son of Hellen, was king of Thessaly and ancestor of the Aeolians.

clue.text: Fantastic course shows leader slipping to fourth place

indicators.note: the first letter slides back to become the fourth, a precise reordering of the letters

explanation.surface: A racecourse puts on a fantastic show when the front runner drops to fourth.
explanation.walkthrough: Leader and fourth place sound like racing, but they describe moving the first letter of ROUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré means bizarre or unconventional, one sense of fantastic.

clue.text: Cold sore for a spell

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Scots dialect word for a cold sore
second meaning: a splinter or fragment, as a spell can be

explanation.walkthrough: Spell looks like a period of time, as in a cold spell; here it is a splinter of wood, another Chambers sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiver is a fragment or splinter, the same as a spell, and in Scots a cold sore.

clue.text: Enjoys a cuppa when one's knocked off? More of it slows you down!

definitions.text: More of it slows you down!

indicators.note: knocked off means removed, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: to have tea is to enjoy a cuppa, British slang for a cup of tea

explanation.surface: Someone sips tea when one of their own is knocked over, and is told to slow down.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the proverb 'more haste, less speed'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says hurrying causes mistakes, so more of this hurry leaves you slower.

clue.text: Bantu speakers back at home with gnus wandering round

indicators.note: back says the word is read in the opposite direction
round says the rearranged animals surround the other piece
wandering animals stray about, so their letters are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: African speakers back home among wandering herds of wildebeest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nguni are a group of southern African peoples, including Zulu and Xhosa, who speak Bantu languages.

clue.text: Hard left when driving in UK

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the side nearer the kerb

explanation.walkthrough: The UK drives on the left, so the nearside is the left-hand side of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: Near can mean mean with money, close to hard, and it names the kerbside of a vehicle, the left in Britain.

clue.text: Boy embraces love willingly

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within the arms, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A son hugs his loved one gladly.
explanation.definitionFit: Soon has an old sense of readily, as in 'I would as soon go', meaning just as willingly.

clue.text: Narrow opening is piercing rocky fault

indicators.note: piercing means going into, so the short word goes inside the other
rocky means unsteady and shaken, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A narrow gap pierces a geological fault in rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A fistula is an abnormal narrow passage in the body, an opening between organs or to the skin.

clue.text: Get out onto platform, but missing right stop

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is left out

parts.note: to detrain is to leave a train

explanation.surface: A passenger gets off at the wrong station and misses the right stop.
explanation.definitionFit: To detain someone is to stop or hold them back.

clue.text: Bulge indicating large corporation round one's middle

indicators.note: round says the word for large wraps around the single letter
the middle of a word is its central letter only

parts.note: the sixth of eleven letters is the centre one

explanation.surface: A bulging waistline indicates a big corporation around one's middle.
explanation.walkthrough: A corporation is old slang for a pot belly, so the surface is about a paunch; 'one's' refers back to the word corporation.
explanation.definitionFit: Strout is a Chambers word meaning to bulge or swell out.

clue.text: What'll separate rowers from back end? Hard frames with man in

definitions.text: What'll separate rowers from back end?

indicators.note: in says the man word goes inside the frames word

parts.note: to set is to frame, as a picture

explanation.surface: Something that keeps oarsmen apart from the stern of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Back end looks like the wordplay for STERN, but it belongs to the definition; Hard gives STERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternsheets is the space in an open boat between the stern and the aftermost rowing thwart.
